title: Containment & Evidence Ledger — RBAC/ SIEM Playbook
content:
Purpose: This runbook focuses on fast containment for RBAC-related incidents, reproducible evidence collection using an evidence ledger pattern, and safe SIEM export procedures. It is written for security on-call and SRE responders who must act quickly to preserve forensic integrity while minimizing operational impact.

Scope: Applies to control-plane incidents (hosted API, console), Dedicated control-plane surfaces, and redwood-managed audit ingestion paths. For private/on-prem customers follow the air-gapped appendix (separate doc).

Quick overview (first 10 minutes):
- Create incident channel: #sec-incident-<ID> and set topic to "holding channel for RBAC incident <ID>".
- Record incident in SEC-INC tracker with incident id and brief one-line summary.
- Run the evidence-ledger bootstrap (single command below) to stamp the incident and create the ledger file.
- Classify: RBAC modification | Suspicious elevated access | Token minting | Service-principal compromise.

Evidence Ledger Pattern (core concept):
- Rationale: keep a machine-readable ledger (CSV or NDJSON) that records every collection action, who did it, and where artifacts are stored. This avoids ad-hoc zip uploads and preserves chain-of-custody.
- Ledger fields (CSV header recommended): incident_id,evidence_uuid,collected_by,collector_version,collection_time_utc,scope,source_path,object_key,sha256,notes
- Ledger filename convention: ledger-<INCIDENT_ID>-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>.csv stored at s3://redwood-security-evidence/incident-<ID>/ledger/
- Bootstrap command (internal helper):
  ./evidence-ledger bootstrap --incident <ID> --owner "<name>" --output s3://redwood-security-evidence/incident-<ID>/ledger/ledger-<ID>-$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%MZ).csv

Containment matrix (decision-first):
- If active privileged change is in progress (role-binding created/updated within last 5m): immediate revocation.
- If suspicious token creation but no observable action: revoke the token, rotate secrets, and block suspect IP ranges.
- If lateral movement or data access seen: isolate affected hosts and escalate to SRE for host snapshot.

Emergency revocation actions (examples):
- Revoke OAuth/OIDC refresh tokens via IdP: Okta session revoke or delete tokens issued. Example API call: POST /api/v1/sessions/{sessionId}/revoke (Okta)
- Revoke API keys in secret manager: use secret-manager rotate-or-disable and annotate ledger with object_key of rotated secret.
- RBAC role-binding revocation (k8s-like): create a minimal deny role or remove subject immediately. Example kubectl snippet:
  kubectl get rolebinding -A | grep "<suspicious-subject>"
  kubectl delete rolebinding <name> -n <namespace>
  # If unsure, apply emergency-readonly-binding (example below)

Forensic snapshot commands (hosts/containers) - run only when authorized and record actions in ledger: 
- Host live capture (Linux):
  sudo mkdir -p /tmp/forensics/<INCIDENT_ID> && sudo tar czf /tmp/forensics/<INCIDENT_ID>/proc-ps-etc.tar.gz /proc /etc /var/log && sha256sum /tmp/forensics/<INCIDENT_ID>/proc-ps-etc.tar.gz
- Container inspect and export:
  docker ps --filter "name=<container>" --format "{{.ID}}" | xargs -I{} docker export {} -o /tmp/<container>-export.tar && sha256sum /tmp/<container>-export.tar
- Kernel and network state: sudo ss -tunap > /tmp/forensics/<INCIDENT_ID>/network-sockets.txt; sudo iptables-save > /tmp/...
- Always upload artifacts to the dedicated S3 evidence path and append ledger entry with object_key and sha256.

Audit slice extraction & SIEM export guidance: 
- Extract a time-bounded slice around the alert (recommended +/- 60 minutes rapid triage, extend once validated). Use audit-exporter tool: 
  ./audit-exporter --from "2025-01-10T12:00:00Z" --to "2025-01-10T13:00:00Z" --filter "action:role_binding.* OR action:token.issue" --output ./slice-<ID>.ndjson
- Normalize fields for SIEM ingestion: map actor.type -> userType, actor.id -> userId, action -> activity, resource -> resourceId, timestamp -> eventTime, request_id -> requestId. Deliver normalized CSV/NDJSON and keep raw in evidence bucket.
- SIEM export filename convention: siem-export-<INCIDENT_ID>-<YYYYMMDDTHHMMZ>.ndjson

Sample SIEM export mapping (flat NDJSON line example):
  {"eventTime":"2025-01-10T12:32:10Z","eventId":"uuid-...","userType":"service","userId":"svc-ingest-1","activity":"role_binding.update","resourceId":"role:admin","srcIp":"1.2.3.4","requestId":"req-...","raw":"..."}

Automated evidence-collector usage (recommended):
- Run collector and immediately record ledger entry: 
  ./evidence-collector --incident <ID> --scopes "audit_slice,cloudtrail,auth_events,container_export" --out s3://redwood-security-evidence/incident-<ID>/raw/
- Collector returns JSON manifest; save that manifest path into the ledger as object_key and capture sha256.

Chain-of-custody (practical steps):
- Every transferred artifact must have: evidence_uuid, collector_user, collection_time_utc, storage_path, sha256, retention_tier. Record these as lines in the ledger CSV.
- Example ledger line: 
  <INCIDENT_ID>,<UUID>,miguel.santos,v1.4,2025-01-10T13:00:00Z,"audit_slice,auth_events","s3://.../slice-<ID>.ndjson","<sha256>","initial triage export"

RBAC change detection quick queries (SIEM/SPL/KQL examples):
- Role-binding creation not by trusted automation:
  index=audits activity="role_binding.create" NOT actor.id IN (gitops-bot,deploy-bot) | table eventTime,userId,resourceId,raw
- Token issuance spikes by service principal:
  index=auth_events activity="token.issue" | stats count by userId,srcIp | where count > 10

Escalation & legal thresholds (short):
- Notify Legal within 1 hour if: PII access detected, customer data accessed, or regulatory scope likely.
- Notify Product / Customer Success if customer-visible data or downtime > 5 minutes.

Communication templates (copyable):
- Slack initial: "SEC P1: RBAC anomaly detected for role=<role> at <time>. Incident <ID>. On-call: @<name>. Channel: #sec-incident-<ID>. Containment started."
- Email to execs (post-contain): subject: "Incident <ID> — RBAC containment summary" body: brief bullets: detection time, containment actions, impact, next steps.

Postmortem ledger-driven template: (fill fields and attach ledger file)
- title: Incident <ID> — concise one-line
- detection_summary: short
- timeline: attach ledger and list major ledger actions (collection, revocation, snapshots) with timestamps
- root_cause: short description
- evidence_references: list of evidence_uuid values and S3 paths (comma-separated)
- impact: systems, customers, data classes
- risk_score: 1-10 (include calculation rationale)
- remediation_plan: short-term (48h), medium (30d), long-term (90d) with owners in format owner:name|due:YYYY-MM-DD|status
- monitoring_changes: detections to add to SIEM with sample queries

Operational tips & guardrails: 
- Never perform destructive host actions (e.g., systemctl stop) unless ordered by SRE lead; prefer snapshot + isolate.
- When rotating secrets at scale, coordinate with CI/CD: use feature flag to avoid mass outage.
- Keep evidence bucket write-only except for authorized auditors; read operations must be logged.

Retention and export rules: 
- Default hot retention: 90 days. If incident is escalated to Legal, retain 1 year in cold tier.
- Exports to third parties: require Legal sign-off and redaction checklist. Record export action in ledger as an entry.

Runbook maintenance: 
- Owner: security-runbooks@redwood.ai; quarterly review cadence. After any usage, the responder must append an entry to the ledger stating which runbook steps were followed and proposed updates.

Appendix (quick snippets):
- Apply emergency-readonly-binding (k8s):
  cat <<EOF | kubectl apply -f -
  apiVersion: rbac.authorization.k8s.io/v1
  kind: RoleBinding
  metadata:
    name: emergency-readonly-binding
    namespace: default
  subjects:
  - kind: Group
    name: emergency-containment
  roleRef:
    kind: Role
    name: readonly-role
    apiGroup: rbac.authorization.k8s.io
  EOF

- Quick audit slice export example: 
  ./audit-exporter --from "2025-01-10T12:00:00Z" --to "2025-01-10T13:00:00Z" --filter "action:role_binding.*" --output /tmp/slice-<ID>.ndjson

Revision history:
- 2024-11-05: initial draft (Miguel Santos)
- 2024-12-02: added ledger bootstrap pattern (Aisha Park)
- 2025-01-12: updated SIEM mapping and postmortem fields (Jordan Lee)

Open action items (working):
- Automate ledger bootstrap as a PagerDuty runbook action.
- Add private-deployment agent instructions for air-gapped evidence transfers.

Contact points: security-oncall@redwood.ai, sec-runbooks@redwood.ai
